THIRD-PARTY NOTICES
===================

Proxyma is made by Le Sy Hau. Proxyma Desktop and Proxyma Home Server (Proxyma Community) are
licensed to you under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3; Proxyma Enterprise Server
is licensed to you under Proxyma's End User License Agreement (https://proxyma.ai/eula). Proxyma
also contains, or downloads on its first start, software made by others. Each of those is
licensed to you under its own license, and nothing in Proxyma's own license limits the rights
those licenses give you. This file lists that software and says where its license texts
are.

  1. Runtimes and programs that come with Proxyma
  2. Java libraries in the application
  3. The web interface
  4. Python packages
  5. Tesseract OCR (Windows)
  6. License texts: Apache License 2.0 and GNU LGPL 2.1
  Source code for GPL and LGPL components - at the end of section 1

The same file is THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt in the installation folder, inside the application, and
in Settings > About > Open-source licenses.

WHERE THINGS ARE. The installation folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Proxyma on Windows and
/opt/proxyma on Linux. What Proxyma downloads on its first start - the application, the Python
runtime, the headless browser and, on Windows, the application window and Tesseract - is kept
in its data folder, one folder per part: %LOCALAPPDATA%\proxyma\parts on Windows and
~/.local/share/proxyma/parts on Linux. In the Docker images (Home Server and Enterprise Server)
the application is in /app and the Java runtime in /opt/java/openjdk.


1. RUNTIMES AND PROGRAMS THAT COME WITH PROXYMA
-----------------------------------------------

Eclipse Temurin Java runtime 21 (OpenJDK) - every edition
  https://adoptium.net
  License: GNU General Public License, version 2, with the Classpath Exception; some of its
  components are under other licenses. Its license texts and notices are in its own legal
  folder: jre\legal in the installation folder (Windows), /opt/proxyma/jre/legal (Linux) and
  /opt/java/openjdk/legal (Docker images).

CPython - document conversion everywhere, and the vector store on Desktop and Home Server
  https://www.python.org
  License: Python Software Foundation License Version 2, with the licenses of the libraries
  CPython includes. On Windows it is python.org's embeddable distribution of 3.13, whose LICENSE.txt is
  in the Python runtime Proxyma builds in its data folder (runtime). On Linux it is a
  python-build-standalone build (https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone), whose
  components and their licenses are listed by that project. In the Docker images it is
  Ubuntu's python3 package, with its copyright file in /usr/share/doc.

Electron 44 - the application window, Desktop
  https://www.electronjs.org
  License: MIT. Electron contains Chromium and the libraries Chromium uses, FFmpeg (GNU LGPL
  2.1 or later) among them. Electron's LICENSE and the notices of everything it contains,
  LICENSES.chromium.html, are beside the window program: in the window part (Windows) or in
  /opt/proxyma/window (Linux).

Chromium headless shell - the browser that renders web pages for web sources, Desktop
  https://www.chromium.org
  License: BSD-3-Clause, with the licenses of the code Chromium contains; its license files are
  in the browser part.

Playwright 1.58 and Node.js - drive that browser, inside the application jar
  https://playwright.dev and https://nodejs.org
  License: Apache-2.0 (Playwright; its LICENSE and NOTICE travel in the driver) and MIT
  (Node.js, with the licenses of the libraries it bundles:
  https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/LICENSE). Both are in the jar's driver-bundle
  library; a desktop build keeps only its own platform's copy.

Tesseract OCR 5.4.0 - offline OCR, Windows Desktop
  See section 5. On Linux and in the Docker images Tesseract is the operating system's own
  tesseract-ocr package, with its copyright file in /usr/share/doc/tesseract-ocr.

Launch4j - proxyma.exe, the Windows launcher
  https://launch4j.sourceforge.net
  License: the executable header proxyma.exe is built from is under the MIT License.

Inno Setup - the Windows installer and uninstaller
  https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php
  License: Inno Setup License.

Orbitron and Space Grotesk - the start-up screen, Desktop
  License: SIL Open Font License 1.1. The fonts and their license texts (OFL.txt,
  OFL-SpaceGrotesk.txt) are in the application jar under fonts/. The web interface's own fonts
  are listed in section 3 with their license.

The Docker images
  Built on eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (Ubuntu 24.04 with the Java runtime above). Every
  operating system package in them carries its copyright file under /usr/share/doc. Their
  Python packages are installed from PyPI when the image is built - a part of section 4
  (Enterprise Server has no ChromaDB) - each with its license in its .dist-info folder under
  /opt/markitdown (Enterprise Server) or /app/python (Home Server).

SOURCE CODE FOR GPL AND LGPL COMPONENTS

Some of the software above is licensed under the GNU General Public License (GPL) or the GNU
Lesser General Public License (LGPL): the Java runtime (GPL-2.0 with the Classpath Exception),
Hibernate ORM in the application jar (LGPL-2.1-or-later), FFmpeg and the other LGPL code in
Electron and in the Chromium headless shell, GNU libiconv in the Windows build of the lxml
Python package (LGPL-2.1-or-later), and JBIG-KIT and GNU libiconv in Tesseract (section 5,
whose own offer is repeated there). Logback and Java Native Access are offered under the LGPL
as one of two licenses; Proxyma uses them under the other (EPL-1.0 and Apache-2.0).

Source code for the components licensed under the GPL or LGPL is available on request at
contact@proxyma.ai for three years from the date you received the software. Name the Proxyma
version you received; it is provided for no more than the cost of performing the
distribution. Most of it is also published by its own project, at the addresses in this file.
